subject.title: fix(agents): deliberate fallback for malformed compaction boundary timestamps

question: Should `AgentSession.checkCompaction` treat malformed or non-positive compaction entry timestamps as unreliable boundaries that skip the stale-message guard?
rationale: The code change is small, but the permanent behavior for corrupted session-state boundaries is a maintainer policy choice rather than a purely mechanical lint or parser fix.

options.title: Accept Unreliable-Boundary Fallback
options.body: Merge this PR’s explicit `undefined` fallback so corrupted boundaries do not suppress compaction and normal checks continue.

options.title: Repair Before Runtime
options.body: Ask for a narrower repair that rejects, migrates, or normalizes corrupted compaction timestamps before `AgentSession` evaluates them.

options.title: Defer To Broader Timestamp Work
options.body: Pause only if a broader timestamp-validation PR becomes the proof-positive replacement for this exact compaction guard surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Unreliable-Boundary Fallback
recommendation.body: Merge this PR’s explicit `undefined` fallback so corrupted boundaries do not suppress compaction and normal checks continue.

likelyOwner.reason: The central session runtime file and feature-history commit make this the best available owner for the fallback-policy choice.
